reframings.new_frame: Autonomous discovery requires bridging the gap between current curiosity-driven task-specific exploration and the long-term longitudinal scalability needed for open-ended scientific inquiry.

reframings.strategy: Focus future research on scalability and longitudinal evaluation metrics to address the identified gap.

reframings.assumptions_changed: Moving from single-agent curiosity exploration to multi-agent co-evolution and structured discrepancy-driven evaluation as core drivers of autonomous inquiry.

reframings.old_frame: Autonomous discovery in artificial agents is achieved by integrating curiosity-driven developmental mechanisms with structured computational creativity frameworks.
reframings.reason: Recent evidence such as CORAL and CVEvolve demonstrates that multi-agent co-evolution and structured separation of evaluation significantly improve autonomous problem discovery and solution quality.
reframings.strategy: Incorporate multi-agent collaboration and discrepancy-driven evaluation as central paradigms for open-ended problem formulation.
